name: Original Xbox
configurations: Thomson / Philips / Samsung DVD drives (Thomson is the weak one).
notes: Clock-capacitor leak is THE signature fault — remove (keeps time only while plugged in) or replace. Weak DVD laser. Avoid: cap leak that already ate nearby traces; modchip-butchered boards.

name: Xbox 360 (Fat)
configurations: Arcade / Pro / Elite; 20/60/120GB HDD.
notes: RROD = GPU/CPU BGA solder failure — walk away as a flip (reflow is temporary). In-lane: PSU, DVD drive, case fan, power-section recap.

name: Xbox 360 Slim / S
configurations: 4GB / 250GB.
notes: Better thermals, no RROD epidemic. In-lane: clean/repaste, HDMI, HDD, ODD, power brick. Avoid: APU BGA.

name: Xbox 360 E
notes: Same profile as Slim — HDMI, drive, fan, HDD, power brick. Avoid: APU BGA (rare).

name: Xbox One (original)
configurations: 500GB / 1TB.
notes: HDMI port (reworkable), Blu-ray drive, external power brick, HDD. Avoid: APU BGA; ODD is serialized to the board — no clean donor-drive swap.

name: Xbox One S
configurations: 500GB / 1TB / 2TB; disc.
notes: Internal PSU (recap-able, no brick), HDMI, storage, fan/thermal. Avoid: APU/GDDR5 BGA reball, serialized ODD.

name: Xbox One X
configurations: 1TB; disc.
notes: Strongest One-gen. HDMI, PSU, storage, fan. Avoid: APU BGA; vapor-chamber / liquid-metal thermal — leave deep thermal jobs early.

name: Xbox Series S
configurations: 512GB / 1TB; digital-only.
notes: Too new for age/cap failures. HDMI, internal/expansion storage, fan, power. Avoid: APU BGA.

name: Xbox Series X
configurations: 1TB; disc.
notes: HDMI port, Blu-ray drive, overheating, PSU, storage. Avoid: APU BGA; serialized disc drive (pairing required).

name: PS1 / original PlayStation
configurations: Multiple board revisions; KSM-440 laser.
notes: KSM-440 laser wear ('only reads upside-down') → laser swap or pot tweak. Recap older boards, lid switch.

name: PS2 (Fat)
configurations: Many revisions; laser sourcing varies by rev.
notes: Disc Read Error is THE fault — worn laser / cracked white worm-gear → gear or laser swap. Recap, power.

name: PS2 Slim
configurations: Slimline revisions.
notes: Laser / DRE, ribbon cables, the flimsy power/reset board (signature Slim failure).

name: PS3 (Fat)
configurations: 20/40/60/80GB; CECHA/CECHC = backward-compatible (collector).
notes: NEC/TOKIN cap replacement (semi-reliable YLOD-adjacent fix), KES-400/410 Blu-ray laser, HDD, repaste. Avoid: YLOD = RSX/Cell BGA (uneconomic). DO NOT part out an early 60GB CECHA/CECHC — worth more whole.

name: PS3 Slim
notes: Repaste, Blu-ray laser, HDD, power. YLOD much rarer than Fat. Avoid: BGA reball.

name: PS3 Super Slim
configurations: 12/250/500GB; top-loader drive.
notes: Top-loader disc-drive belt/gear, laser, HDD, power. Avoid: BGA (rare).

name: PS4 (original)
configurations: 500GB / 1TB.
notes: HDMI port (very common bread-and-butter rework), Blu-ray drive, PSU (Blue Light of Death is often PSU or HDMI handshake), HDD, fan, power-button board. Avoid: APU BGA, severe liquid damage.

name: PS4 Slim
configurations: 500GB / 1TB.
notes: HDMI, drive, PSU, HDD, fan. Avoid: APU BGA.

name: PS4 Pro
configurations: 1TB.
notes: HDMI, overheating (loud-fan → clean/repaste), PSU, drive, storage. Avoid: APU BGA.

name: PS5 (disc)
configurations: 825GB; disc.
notes: HDMI port = the #1 PS5 fault (cable-yanked, hot-air rework), fan/thermal, no-power/beep, power section. Avoid: APU BGA, liquid-metal spread, serialized disc drive (donor needs pairing).

name: PS5 Digital
configurations: 825GB; digital (no disc drive).
notes: HDMI, fan, power, thermal. No disc drive to deal with. Avoid: APU BGA, liquid metal.

name: PS5 Slim
configurations: 1TB; detachable (paired) disc drive.
notes: HDMI, thermal, power; detachable disc drive is paired. Avoid: APU BGA.

name: PS5 Pro
configurations: 2TB; digital, optional add-on disc drive.
notes: Newest — parts scarce/expensive, barely in the repair channel. HDMI, thermal, power. Avoid: APU BGA; high unit cost makes any risk expensive.

name: Xbox 360 Wireless Controller
configurations: AA battery pack (no internal LiPo).
notes: Stick drift (module reflow), worn bumpers/triggers, battery-contact corrosion, sticky buttons. Avoid: RF/sync-board failure (not worth it on a cheap pad).

name: Xbox One Wireless Controller (original)
configurations: No Bluetooth, no 3.5mm jack.
notes: Stick drift, micro-USB charge port, bumper switches, button membrane. Avoid: board/pairing-IC faults.

name: Xbox One Wireless Controller (2016 / "S")
configurations: Added Bluetooth + 3.5mm headset jack.
notes: Stick drift, micro-USB port, bumpers, membrane, headset jack. Buyers often can't tell it from the 2013 pad — listings blur them. Model 1708 is the on-label number.

name: Xbox Elite Wireless Controller Series 1
configurations: Paddles, swappable sticks/d-pad.
notes: Stick drift, micro-USB charge port, bumpers, paddle/trigger-lock mechanics. Avoid: mainboard faults (lower ceiling than Series 2).

name: Xbox Elite Wireless Controller Series 2
configurations: USB-C, internal LiPo, paddles.
notes: Stick drift (module swap), the infamous bumper microswitch failure (very common, in-lane), USB-C port, LiPo swap, paddle mechanics. High ceiling — moderate board jobs can pencil out.

name: Xbox Series X|S Wireless Controller
configurations: USB-C; share button. Cross-compatible with Xbox One.
notes: Stick drift, USB-C charge port, bumpers, button membrane. Listings mix generations. Avoid: board/pairing faults.

name: DualShock 3
configurations: Internal LiPo (old units = dead/puffy).
notes: Stick drift, mini-USB charge port, LiPo battery swap, sticky buttons, conductive-pad refresh. Avoid: board/BT faults, puffy-battery board damage.

name: DualShock 4 (v1)
configurations: Light bar on front only.
notes: Stick drift (the headline DS4 fault), micro-USB charge port (very common), LiPo swap, bumper/trigger switches, touchpad. Avoid: mainboard/BT-IC faults.

name: DualShock 4 (v2)
configurations: Light strip visible on the touchpad; later 3.5mm/USB audio.
notes: Same as v1 — stick drift, micro-USB port, battery, bumpers — plus the touchpad light strip. Avoid: mainboard/BT faults.

name: DualSense (PS5)
configurations: USB-C, internal LiPo, adaptive triggers.
notes: Stick drift (endemic — class-action territory), USB-C charge port, LiPo swap, adaptive-trigger mechanism (springy/broken L2-R2), bumpers. Avoid: adaptive-trigger driver-IC / mainboard, liquid damage.

name: DualSense Edge
configurations: User-replaceable stick modules, back buttons, swappable caps.
notes: Stick drift — but sticks are user-replaceable modules, so the fix is often trivial; USB-C port, LiPo swap, back-button/trigger mechanics. Avoid: mainboard/BT-IC (high ceiling can still justify it).

name: VG27AQ
configurations: 27" 1440p; external 19V DC brick; ~2 internal boards (main/scaler + probable backlight/inverter).
notes: External brick offloads the PSU → fewer internal boards. First completed board-level repair: a recap fixed the bootloop. (Year fetched, not in the taxonomy doc.)

name: Predator XB271HU
configurations: 27" 1440p G-Sync; internal PSU (IEC mains); 4 boards incl. NVIDIA G-Sync module. bmiprz variant 2017.
notes: Mains-direct → internal PSU + more boards. Hardware G-Sync FPGA module is the priciest/most proprietary part (subsumes the scaler). WLED boost (MP3398A) lives on the PSU board. (Year fetched.)

name: Wii U (Deluxe)
configurations: 8GB Basic (white, WUP-001); 32GB Deluxe/Premium (black, WUP-101); bundled GamePad (WUP-010)
notes: GamePad is the weak point: digitizer/LCD cracks and GamePad battery (swappable) are the bread-and-butter fixes; GamePad won't re-pair to a new console board easily (paired to the Wii U). Console side: failing eMMC/NAND and HDMI port rework are common. Disc-drive gear/laser wear. Avoid the multi-chip MCM (Espresso/Latte) reball. Solid recap/port-rework lane, weak resale ceiling.

name: Nintendo 2DS
configurations: 4GB microSD bundle standard; entry-level non-clamshell wedge; no 3D; single-LCD-behind-glass
notes: Top digitizer/touch glass cracks (single sheet over both screens) and the slide power switch are the common faults; both LCDs and the digitizer are cheap, abundant swaps. Charge port (4-pin) reflows. SD-card-based OS, so no eMMC pairing headache. Hinge-less = fewer ribbon-fatigue failures than clamshell 3DS. Easy beginner repair platform, low resale.

name: New Nintendo 3DS
configurations: 4GB microSD; swappable cover plates; C-stick + ZL/ZR; NA standard model via bundles
notes: Clamshell ribbon cables through the hinge fail (top-screen lines/backlight) — fiddly but fixable. Top IPS-vs-TN LCD lottery on swaps. C-stick (rubber nub) and circle-pad wear; charge port reflow. Battery swaps easy. Cover-plate design makes teardown friendlier than older 3DS. Avoid chasing intermittent motherboard NAND faults. Smaller NA supply bumps resale vs the XL.

name: New Nintendo 3DS XL
configurations: 4GB microSD; larger 4.88"/4.18" screens; C-stick + ZL/ZR; no swappable face plates (NA)
notes: Most common 3DS in the channel. Hinge ribbon-cable fatigue (top screen lines/dead backlight) is THE fault — replace the flex, not the board. Top LCD cracks; cheap LCD + digitizer swaps. Circle-pad and charge-port (reflow/replace) wear. Battery swap trivial. Avoid board-level NAND/CPU work; abundant donor units make whole-board swap cheaper. Strong, steady resale.

name: New Nintendo 2DS XL
configurations: 4GB microSD; clamshell, no 3D; C-stick + ZL/ZR; XL-size screens
notes: Same hinge-ribbon failure mode as New 3DS XL (top-screen lines) — replace the flex cable. Top LCD/digitizer crack swaps are cheap. Circle-pad nub and charge-port reflow. Lighter plastic clamshell, easy battery swap. SD-based OS, no eMMC pairing. Avoid board-level NAND chases; donor units plentiful. Good resale, well-liked final 3DS-family unit.

name: Nintendo Switch (original)
configurations: 32GB internal; launch HAC-001 lower battery; 2019 HAC-001(-01) is the better-battery red-box refresh; neon/gray Joy-Con
notes: Joy-Con drift is the signature fault — analog-stick module is a cheap solder-in swap (no pairing). Console-side: USB-C charge port rework (very common, lifted pads) and the M92T36 charge IC / P13USB video IC are the classic board-level repairs. eMMC failures recoverable. Beware patched/early units bricking. Launch HAC-001 is the patchable unit hobbyists value. Excellent repair lane, deep parts/donor supply.

name: Nintendo Switch Lite
configurations: 32GB internal; handheld-only (non-detachable controls); no TV-out/dock; gray/yellow/turquoise/coral/blue
notes: Built-in stick drift is THE fault and worse here because the stick is soldered to the mainboard — module swap requires desoldering (more skill than Joy-Con but very common bench work). USB-C charge port rework frequent. M92T36/charge-IC faults like the big Switch. Screen/digitizer cracks cheap to swap. No detachable parts = every drift fix is a teardown. High repair volume, steady resale.

name: Nintendo Switch OLED
configurations: 64GB internal; 7" OLED screen; wide adjustable stand; dock with wired LAN; white or neon blue/red
notes: Joy-Con drift still the headline fault — stick module swap, no pairing (same as original Switch). Console-side USB-C port rework and M92T36/P13USB board-level repair carry over. OLED panel swaps are pricier than the LCD units — assess panel cost before quoting. eMMC recoverable. Best resale of the Switch family; charge-port + Joy-Con work is the profitable lane, OLED panel replacement the judgment call.

name: Steam Deck (LCD)
configurations: 64GB eMMC / 256GB NVMe / 512GB NVMe (anti-glare); 7" LCD; user-replaceable M.2 2230 SSD
notes: Stick drift (Hall-effect-upgradeable thumbstick modules — popular mod/repair) and worn analog sticks. USB-C port rework common (it's the only port). Fan rattle/replacement and SSD (M.2 2230) swaps are easy, sanctioned repairs — iFixit-friendliest handheld. Cracked LCD/digitizer swaps. Avoid the soldered APU/RAM. Great repairability, strong resale, deep parts ecosystem.

name: Steam Deck OLED
configurations: 512GB / 1TB NVMe; 7.4" HDR OLED 90Hz; larger 50Wh battery; Wi-Fi 6E; user-replaceable M.2 2230 SSD
notes: Same repair-friendly platform as the LCD: Hall-effect-mod thumbstick swaps for drift, easy fan and M.2 2230 SSD replacement, single USB-C port rework. OLED panel swaps cost more than the LCD unit — price the panel before committing. Larger battery is a clean swap. Avoid soldered APU/RAM. Best-in-class handheld repairability; strongest resale of the PC handhelds.

name: ROG Ally
configurations: 512GB NVMe; Ryzen Z1 or Z1 Extreme; 7" 1080p 120Hz; Windows; M.2 2230 SSD; microSD slot
notes: Infamous microSD reader failure — slot sits near the APU exhaust and cooks; dead/erratic card readers are the signature fault (often a whole-board or reader-mod fix). Stick drift and USB-C/charge-port rework common. SSD (M.2 2230) user-swappable. Fan/thermal cleaning routine. Cracked screen swaps. Avoid soldered LPDDR5/APU work. The SD-reader reputation depresses prices.

name: Legion Go
configurations: 256GB/512GB/1TB NVMe; Ryzen Z1 Extreme; 8.8" QHD+ 144Hz; detachable controllers; Windows; M.2 2242 SSD
notes: Detachable controllers (Switch-like) mean stick-drift fixes can be done at the controller without opening the tablet — but the sticks are Hall-effect, so true drift is rarer; connector/rail wear more likely. USB-C charge-port rework. SSD is the less-common M.2 2242 — verify size before ordering. Hinge/kickstand and fan service. Cracked large QHD panel swaps are pricey. Avoid soldered RAM/APU. Reasonable resale.

name: Nintendo Switch 2
configurations: 256GB internal (UFS); 7.9" 1080p 120Hz LCD; magnetic Joy-Con 2; dock BEE-053; microSD Express only
notes: Too new to have a settled fault profile — treat cautiously. Expect class faults to carry: Joy-Con 2 stick drift (now magnetic-attach controllers, so module/controller-level swap likely) and USB-C charge-port rework. Board-level charge-IC repair analogous to Gen-1 Switch probable. microSD Express requirement is a support headache, not a repair. Avoid speculative BGA work; parts/donor supply still thin.

name: VG248QE
configurations: 24" 1080p; TN; 144Hz; 1ms; WLED; internal PSU (IEC mains)
notes: Class faults: dead backlight (open WLED string / boost FET on power board), bulging caps on power/inverter section, dead OSD button board, stuck-in-standby. Internal mains PSU => power board + scaler + panel-drive boards inside; mains caps are first suspect.

name: VG278HE
configurations: 27" 1080p; TN; 144Hz; 2ms; WLED; internal PSU
notes: First 144Hz-class panel. Class faults: WLED backlight string open (image present under flashlight but dark), bad caps on internal power board, T-con/panel-drive, dead button board. Internal mains PSU => multi-board; check primary/secondary electrolytics.

name: ROG Swift PG278Q
configurations: 27" 1440p; TN; 144Hz; G-Sync (hardware module); internal PSU
notes: Hardware G-Sync module adds a board beyond scaler/T-con. Class faults: backlight boost / WLED open, power-board caps, dead OSD joystick board, no-POST from G-Sync module. Internal mains PSU => several stacked boards.

name: ROG Swift PG279Q
configurations: 27" 1440p; IPS (AHVA); 165Hz; hardware G-Sync; internal PSU
notes: Class faults: WLED backlight string open (dark panel, backlight dead), power-board electrolytic failure, T-con, hardware G-Sync module no-POST, dead joystick/OSD board. Internal mains PSU => high internal board count.

name: ProArt PA248Q
configurations: 24" 1920x1200 (16:10); IPS; 60Hz; WLED; internal PSU; 4-port USB 3.0 hub
notes: Office/creator panel. Class faults: WLED backlight open, power-board caps, T-con, dead USB-hub board, OSD board. Internal mains PSU => power + scaler + hub boards. USB hub adds a failure-prone daughterboard.

name: VG279Q
configurations: 27" 1080p; IPS; 144Hz; FreeSync; internal PSU
notes: Class faults: WLED edge-lit backlight string open (dark image, backlight dead), power-board electrolytic failure, T-con, dead OSD/button board, stuck-in-standby. Internal mains PSU => power + scaler boards.

name: VG258Q
configurations: 24.5" 1080p; TN; 144Hz; FreeSync; internal PSU
notes: Class faults: WLED backlight string open, bad caps on power board, T-con/panel-drive, dead OSD board, standby-lock from power section. Internal mains PSU => multi-board layout.

name: VG245H
configurations: 24" 1080p; TN; 75Hz; FreeSync; dual HDMI (console); external power brick (DC-in)
notes: External brick => no mains PSU inside; fewer internal boards (scaler/T-con + LED driver). Class faults: dead/weak brick (check DC first), WLED backlight string open, boost-converter fault on LED driver, dead button board.

name: Predator XB241H
configurations: 24" 1080p; TN; 144Hz (180Hz OC); hardware G-Sync; internal PSU
notes: Hardware G-Sync board present. Class faults: WLED backlight string open, power-board caps, T-con, G-Sync module no-POST, dead OSD/joystick board. Internal mains PSU => stacked boards.

name: Predator XB241YU
configurations: 23.8" 1440p; IPS (AHVA); 144Hz (165Hz OC); hardware G-Sync; internal PSU
notes: Class faults: WLED backlight string open (dark panel), power-board electrolytic failure, T-con, hardware G-Sync no-POST, dead joystick board. Internal mains PSU => high internal board count.

name: Nitro VG240Y
configurations: 23.8" 1080p; IPS; 75Hz; FreeSync; external power brick (DC-in)
notes: Very high-volume budget office/gaming resale. External brick => check DC supply first; few internal boards (scaler/T-con + LED driver). Class faults: dead brick, WLED string open, LED-driver boost fault, dead button board.

name: Nitro VG271U
configurations: 27" 1440p; IPS; 144Hz; FreeSync; HDR400; internal PSU
notes: Class faults: WLED backlight string open (dark image, backlight dead), power-board caps, T-con, dead OSD board, stuck-in-standby. Internal mains PSU => power + scaler boards.

name: UltraSharp U2415
configurations: 24.1" 1920x1200 (16:10); IPS; 60Hz; WLED; internal PSU; USB hub
notes: Workhorse office panel, extremely common resale. Class faults: WLED backlight open, power-board electrolytic failure, T-con, dead USB-hub/OSD board. Internal mains PSU => power + scaler + hub boards.

name: UltraSharp U2719D
configurations: 27" 1440p; IPS; 60Hz; WLED; internal PSU (non-USB-C variant)
notes: Class faults: WLED backlight string open, power-board caps, T-con, dead OSD board. Internal mains PSU => power + scaler boards. (U2719DC is the USB-C sibling.)

name: UltraSharp U2719DC (USB-C)
configurations: 27" 1440p; IPS; 60Hz; WLED; USB-C (65W PD) + USB hub; internal PSU
notes: USB-C PD adds a power-delivery daughterboard (common failure: no charge / no video over Type-C). Other class faults: WLED string open, power-board caps, T-con, dead hub/OSD board. Internal mains PSU.

name: S2716DG
configurations: 27" 1440p; TN; 144Hz; hardware G-Sync; internal PSU
notes: Hardware G-Sync board present. Class faults: WLED backlight string open, power-board electrolytic failure, T-con, G-Sync module no-POST, dead OSD board. Internal mains PSU => stacked boards.

name: S2417DG

notes: Hardware G-Sync board present. Class faults: WLED backlight string open, power-board caps, T-con, G-Sync no-POST, dead OSD/button board. Internal mains PSU => high internal board count.

name: SE2417HG
configurations: 23.6" 1080p; TN; 60Hz (HDMI); budget office/gaming; external power brick (DC-in)
notes: External brick => check DC supply first; minimal internal boards (scaler/T-con + LED driver). Class faults: dead brick, WLED string open, LED-driver boost fault, dead button board. High-volume cheap resale unit.

name: MacBook Air 13" (Intel, Early 2014)
configurations: 13.3" 1440x900; Core i5/i7 Haswell; 4-8GB LPDDR3 (soldered); 128-512GB PCIe SSD (proprietary, removable)
notes: Common: MagSafe 2 DC-in board (cheap, connectorized), battery swell/swap, trackpad, screen hinge/flex, liquid damage. SSD is a removable proprietary blade (upgradeable w/ adapter); RAM soldered. A1466 spans 2013-2017 refreshes - check EMC. No butterfly keyboard (reliable scissor).
